title: Looking for an apartment
goal: Read Québec apartment ads, decode their abbreviations (4 ½, chauffé, éclairé, semi-meublé…), and call a landlord to ask about an apartment.

items.en: rent (the monthly payment for a home)

example.fr: Le loyer est de 1450 $ par mois.

items.note: Literally “heated”. The opposite in ads: n/c (non chauffé).

example.en: Heating is included in the rent.

items.note: Literally “lit”. The opposite in ads: n/é (non éclairé), so you pay the electricity bill yourself.

example.fr: Le 4 ½ est chauffé et éclairé.
example.en: Heating and electricity are included in the 4 ½.

items.note: Short for les électroménagers: fridge, stove, washer, dryer…
Same word for a woman: la propriétaire. Informal: le proprio.
The usual word in Québec. In France, people usually say le parking.

accept: Est-ce que l'appartement est toujours disponible ?
Est-ce que l'appartement est encore disponible ?
Qu'est-ce qui est inclus dans le loyer ?

items.fr: Est-ce que je pourrais visiter l'appartement ?
items.en: Could I see the apartment? (asking to visit, polite)
accept: Est-ce que je peux visiter l'appartement ?

items.en: talking about the rent: le loyer est de… / c'est… par mois

drills.explain: After [[le loyer est]], put [[de]] before the amount.
Spoken French often puts the question word at the end: [[Le loyer est de combien ?]]

steps.title: Apartment hunting in Montréal
steps.intro: Amira and her brother need a two-bedroom apartment. She reads three ads on a rental website, then calls a landlord.

blocks.title: Three ads
blocks.context: Real Québec ads are short and full of abbreviations. Read them once for the general idea; the next step decodes everything.
blocks.fr:
Annonce 1 — Rosemont : 4 ½ rénové au 2e étage, près du métro. Chauffé, éclairé, semi-meublé, électros inclus. Libre le 1er juillet. Bail de 12 mois. 1450 $ par mois. Pas d'animaux.
Annonce 2 — Villeray : grand 4 ½ au rez-de-chaussée, n/c n/é. Entrée laveuse-sécheuse. Stationnement inclus. Libre maintenant. 1250 $ par mois.
Annonce 3 — Plateau : 3 ½ meublé au 3e étage, avec balcon. Chauffé. Idéal pour étudiant. 1150 $ par mois. Libre le 1er août.
blocks.en:
Ad 1 — Rosemont: renovated 4 ½ on the 2nd floor, near the metro. Heating and electricity included, semi-furnished, appliances included. Available July 1. 12-month lease. $1,450 a month. No pets.
Ad 2 — Villeray: large 4 ½ on the ground floor, heating and electricity not included. Washer-dryer hookups. Parking included. Available now. $1,250 a month.
Ad 3 — Plateau: furnished 3 ½ on the 3rd floor, with balcony. Heating included. Ideal for a student. $1,150 a month. Available August 1.

blocks.prompt: Amira doesn't want to pay electricity and heating bills. Which ad suits her best?
blocks.explain: Only ad 1 says [[chauffé, éclairé]]: both heating and electricity are included. Ad 2 is [[n/c n/é]] (not included), and ad 3 is only [[chauffé]].
optionFeedback: [[n/c n/é]] means non chauffé, non éclairé: she would pay both bills herself.
Ad 3 is only [[chauffé]] (heating), and it's a 3 ½ with one bedroom.

blocks.prompt: Amira needs two bedrooms. Which apartment is too small?
blocks.explain: In Québec, a [[3 ½]] has one bedroom; a [[4 ½]] has two. The next step explains how the numbers work.

blocks.title: Amira calls about ad 1
blocks.context: Amira phones the landlord, Mr. Tremblay. She uses vous: it's a formal situation.

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.fr: Bonjour, monsieur. J'ai vu votre annonce pour le quatre et demie à Rosemont. Est-ce que l'appartement est toujours disponible ?
lines.en: Hello, sir. I saw your ad for the 4 ½ in Rosemont. Is the apartment still available?

lines.speaker: M. Tremblay
lines.fr: Oui, il est libre à partir du premier juillet.

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.fr: Parfait. Le loyer est de mille quatre cent cinquante dollars par mois, c'est ça ? Qu'est-ce qui est inclus ?
lines.en: Perfect. The rent is $1,450 a month, is that right? What's included?

lines.speaker: M. Tremblay
lines.fr: C'est chauffé et éclairé, donc le chauffage et l'électricité sont inclus. Et c'est semi-meublé : il y a un frigo et une cuisinière.
lines.en: Heating and electricity are included. And it's semi-furnished: there's a fridge and a stove.

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.fr: Est-ce qu'il y a une laveuse et une sécheuse ?
lines.en: Is there a washer and a dryer?

lines.speaker: M. Tremblay
lines.fr: Non, mais il y a une salle de lavage au sous-sol. Le bail est d'un an, du premier juillet au trente juin.
lines.en: No, but there's a laundry room in the basement. The lease is for one year, from July 1 to June 30.

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.fr: D'accord. Est-ce que je pourrais visiter l'appartement cette semaine ?
lines.en: OK. Could I see the apartment this week?

lines.speaker: M. Tremblay
lines.fr: Bien sûr. Vous êtes libre jeudi à 18 h ?
lines.en: Of course. Are you free on Thursday at 6 p.m.?

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.fr: Oui, jeudi, c'est parfait. Je m'appelle Amira Benali. Merci beaucoup, monsieur, et à jeudi !
lines.en: Yes, Thursday is perfect. My name is Amira Benali. Thank you very much, sir, see you on Thursday!

blocks.body: Notice how Amira prepares her questions: availability, rent, what's included, appliances, the lease, and a visit. That's the checklist for any call about an apartment.

blocks.title: How Québec counts rooms
blocks.body:
In Québec, an apartment is named by its **number of rooms**: [[un 3 ½]], [[un 4 ½]] (say [[un trois et demie]], [[un quatre et demie]]). Bedrooms, the living room and the kitchen each count as **one** room. The bathroom counts as a **half**.

So the quick rule is: **number − 2 = bedrooms**. A [[4 ½]] has two bedrooms; a [[5 ½]] has three.

blocks.title: Apartment sizes
head: Ad
Say
What you get
rows: a studio: one room with a kitchenette, plus a bathroom
one main room + a separate kitchen + a bathroom
blocks.note: Elsewhere in Canada, people say *a one-bedroom*, *a two-bedroom*. In France, ads use [[un T2]], [[un T3]]… where the number counts the main rooms only (living room + bedrooms): a T3 is like a Québec 4 ½.

blocks.title: What the ads say
head: In the ad
In full
Meaning
rows: you pay heating and electricity yourself
hookups for your own washer and dryer

blocks.title: Questions to ask a landlord
blocks.note: You already know these question forms from A1. Here they are, ready for a phone call. Use **vous** with a landlord.

examples.fr: Est-ce que les animaux sont acceptés ?
Il y a combien de chambres ?
Est-ce que je pourrais visiter l'appartement ?

blocks.body:
- **False friend:** [[une location]] is a *rental*, not a location. [[Un appartement en location]] = an apartment for rent. A place is [[un endroit]].
- [[Une chambre]] is a **bedroom**. Any room is [[une pièce]]: [[un 4 ½, c'est quatre pièces et demie]].
- [[Éclairé]] in an ad doesn't mean *bright*. A bright apartment is [[lumineux]].
- Say [[le loyer est **de** 1450 $]] and [[1450 $ **par** mois]].
- [[Qu'est-ce qui est inclus ?]] uses **qui**, because *what* is the subject of the verb here. Learn it as a chunk for now.

blocks.title: Moving day and the lease in Québec
blocks.body:
- **July 1st** ([[le 1er juillet]]) is Québec's unofficial moving day. It's a tradition, not a law: many leases run from July 1 to June 30, so thousands of households move on the same day. Book a truck early! In spring, you'll hear [[Tu déménages le 1er juillet ?]] everywhere.
- [[Le bail]] in Québec is usually written on a **standard form**, and the **TAL** ([[Tribunal administratif du logement]]) is the public body that handles disputes between landlords and tenants.
- Rules on deposits, rent increases and lease renewals are specific to Québec and they change from time to time. Check [[tal.gouv.qc.ca]] or ask a housing committee ([[un comité logement]]) before you sign.
- People say [[l'Hydro]] for the electricity bill, from Hydro-Québec: [[C'est n/é, donc tu paies l'Hydro.]]

blocks.title: Listen and repeat
blocks.note: Say each line as if you were on the phone with a landlord.

lines.tip: Say it smoothly, like one long word.
Let your voice rise at the end: it's a question.

lines.fr: Le bail commence le premier juillet.
Est-ce que je pourrais visiter l'appartement ?

blocks.fr: Bonjour, ici Nathalie Roy. Je vous rappelle pour le cinq et demie de la rue Masson. L'appartement est chauffé, mais il n'est pas éclairé. Le loyer est de mille six cents dollars par mois.
blocks.en: Hello, this is Nathalie Roy. I'm calling you back about the 5 ½ on Masson Street. Heating is included, but electricity isn't. The rent is $1,600 a month.
blocks.prompt: A landlord leaves you a voicemail. What will you have to pay yourself?
blocks.explain: [[chauffé]] = heating included; [[il n'est pas éclairé]] = electricity not included, so you pay the electricity bill.

blocks.fr: Ah, désolé, madame. J'ai déjà trouvé un locataire la semaine dernière.
blocks.en: Oh, sorry, madam. I already found a tenant last week.
blocks.prompt: What does the landlord tell you?
options: The apartment will be available next week.
He is looking for a new landlord.
blocks.explain: [[J'ai déjà trouvé un locataire]] = I've already found a tenant (passé composé), so the apartment is gone.

blocks.fr: Le loyer est de mille deux cents dollars par mois.
accept: Le loyer est de 1200 $ par mois.
Le loyer est de 1200 dollars par mois.
Le loyer est de 1 200 $ par mois.
Le loyer est de 1 200 dollars par mois.
blocks.explain: [[mille deux cents]]: no -s on mille, but cents takes an -s when it ends the number. Digits are fine too.

blocks.prompt: Match the ad words to their meaning.
Karim, his wife and their two children need three bedrooms. What should he look for?
blocks.explain: Number − 2 = bedrooms: a [[5 ½]] has three bedrooms.
optionFeedback: A 4 ½ has only two bedrooms.
A 3 ½ has only one bedroom.

blocks.text: Le ___ est de 1450 $ par mois, et le ___ commence le 1er juillet.
blocks.en: The rent is $1,450 a month, and the lease starts on July 1.
blocks.explain: [[le loyer]] = the money you pay each month; [[le bail]] = the contract. [[La location]] means rental, in general.

accept: Est-ce que l'appartement est toujours disponible ?
Est-ce que l'appartement est encore disponible ?
blocks.explain: [[toujours]] means *always*, but also *still*: [[Il est toujours disponible ?]]

blocks.text: Bonjour, monsieur. J'___ ___ votre annonce sur Internet.
blocks.en: Hello, sir. I saw your ad online.
blocks.explain: Passé composé of [[voir]]: [[j'ai vu]]. This is the classic first line of a call about an ad.

accept: Qu'est-ce qui est inclus dans le loyer ?
Dans le loyer, qu'est-ce qui est inclus ?
blocks.explain: [[Qu'est-ce qui]] + verb: *what* is the subject here. [[Dans le loyer]] = in the rent.

blocks.prompt: The ad says “4 ½, n/c n/é, 1250 $”. Mei says the rent is cheap. What should she keep in mind?
options: She will also pay for heating and electricity.
blocks.explain: [[n/c n/é]] = non chauffé, non éclairé. In winter, heating can add a lot to the monthly cost.

blocks.prompt: We will move on July 1. (use the futur simple)
blocks.explain: Futur simple of a regular -er verb: infinitive + ending → [[nous déménagerons]]. The first of the month is [[le 1er]] (premier).

blocks.text: Pour visiter l'appartement, il ___ appeler le propriétaire avant jeudi.
blocks.en: To see the apartment, you have to call the landlord before Thursday.
blocks.explain: [[Il faut]] + infinitive = you have to / it's necessary to (A2 unit 6).

blocks.fr: Le bail commence le premier juillet.
blocks.explain: [[bail]] ends in -ail, like [[travail]]. [[Le premier]] (1er) is the only date that uses an ordinal number.

blocks.prompt: Call the landlord of ad 2 (the 4 ½ in Villeray, n/c n/é, 1250 $). Greet them, say you saw the ad, check that it's still available, ask what's included and if pets are allowed, and ask to visit. Imagine the answers.
checklist: Greeting with vous: Bonjour, madame / monsieur
What's included: Qu'est-ce qui est inclus ?
One more question (pets, parking, appliances, the lease)
Ask to visit with a day and time

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Bonjour, madame. J'ai vu votre annonce pour le quatre et demie à Villeray. Est-ce qu'il est toujours disponible ? … Super. Qu'est-ce qui est inclus ? … Le stationnement, d'accord. Et est-ce que les animaux sont acceptés ? J'ai un petit chat. … Est-ce que je pourrais visiter l'appartement samedi matin ? … Parfait. Je m'appelle Raj Patel. Merci, madame, à samedi !
models.en: Hello, madam. I saw your ad for the 4 ½ in Villeray. Is it still available? … Great. What's included? … Parking, OK. And are pets allowed? I have a small cat. … Could I see the apartment on Saturday morning? … Perfect. My name is Raj Patel. Thank you, madam, see you on Saturday! (The … mark the landlord's answers.)

blocks.prompt: Write a text message to a friend about an apartment you're going to visit: its size, the neighbourhood, the rent, what's included, when it's available and when you'll visit.
checklist: Rent: Le loyer est de… par mois
Your visit with aller + infinitive or the futur simple

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Salut Lucie ! J'ai trouvé un 4 ½ à Rosemont, près du métro. Le loyer est de 1450 $ par mois, mais c'est chauffé et éclairé, et les électros sont inclus. Il est libre le 1er juillet. Je vais visiter l'appartement jeudi soir. Tu veux venir avec moi ?
models.en: Hi Lucie! I found a 4 ½ in Rosemont, near the metro. The rent is $1,450 a month, but heating and electricity are included, and the appliances are included. It's available on July 1. I'm going to see the apartment on Thursday evening. Do you want to come with me?

summary:
- Decode Québec apartment ads: [[4 ½]], [[chauffé]], [[éclairé]], [[n/c n/é]], [[semi-meublé]], [[électros inclus]], [[libre le 1er juillet]]
- Talk about [[le loyer]] and [[le bail]], and know why July 1 matters in Québec
- Call a landlord: [[L'appartement est toujours disponible ?]], [[Qu'est-ce qui est inclus ?]], [[Est-ce que je pourrais visiter l'appartement ?]]
